title: Lesson 8: Designing Tools That Fail Well: Schemas, Error Handling, and Retries
description: A tool is an operational contract, not an API wrapper. This lesson covers the five-part anatomy of a production tool, structured error schemas the model can act on, and retry discipline (backoff with jitter, idempotency keys, and retry budgets), so agents survive failures without corrupting state.

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the lesson’s guidance?
options: The one idea to take from this lesson: a tool schema is an operational contract between the model, your application layer, and the system being accessed, and the error path is part of that contract, not an afterthought.
Enterprise agents are connected to production systems, and a vague schema or a blind retry can cause wrong reports, duplicate orders, or operational disruption.

This lesson is about the tools themselves: what separates a demo tool from a production tool is not the happy path; it's how the tool behaves when something goes wrong.
